attrs.evidence: docs/spec/proof-wire/experiment/holdout_schema.mjs, a validator for the subset those two documents use, written rather than imported so the clean-room implementer can audit it in an afternoon. fixtures/synthetic-negatives.json carries 16 documents that must each be REFUSED, one per boundary rule -- a fixture whose every case is accepted cannot tell a validator from a pass-through, which is what P4.6's was. Gate `gov-nest`; grid boolean scorer-implementation-free.
attrs.statement: A SCHEMA THAT DOCUMENTS A BOUNDARY NOBODY EXECUTES IS PROSE. P4.6 published holdout-observation-v1.schema.json and never ran it. MEASURED: adding a forbidden member to the envelope, a forbidden member to an observation and a forbidden member to a node record -- all three refused by additionalProperties:false -- left the document ACCEPTED and the result an unchanged 8/8/3. Every observation document is validated against that schema, and every challenge against holdout-recipe-v1.schema.json, BEFORE scoring; an unknown member, a malformed root, a duplicated or unsorted refusal code, a wrong type, a wrong envelope or a spec_release_id that is not the run's release is REFUSED rather than scored. Sortedness is enforced by an EXTENSION keyword named as such, because vanilla JSON Schema cannot express it and a refusal set is compared for exact set equality by byte-comparing sorted arrays -- an unsorted one is not a differently-presented set, it is a set that compares unequal to itself.
